description:
FILED s429 (Fable), found by the #259 matrix.  PRE-EXISTING.

  use feature "signatures";
  sub f ($x) { "f($x)" }
  my $x = f 5;          # perl: f(5)     PCL: Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'x' captured by sub f
  print "$x\n";

The same with `sub f ($x = 1)` and `sub f ($x, @r)`.  The file-lexical capture detector
sees `$x` used inside sub f and a file-level `my $x` and calls it a capture; a signature
parameter is a declaration INSIDE the sub (perl desugars it to `my $x = $_[0]`), so the
body's `$x` is the param, never the file lexical â and the file `my $x` is declared AFTER
the sub anyway.  Check whether the v2 signature lowering registers its params with the
same scope machinery a body-level `my` uses (VarAnnotator / the capture resolver), or
whether the detector walks the body without the signature's declarations.  Task #125
(s316b) de-gated "file lexical captured by sub" when a SHADOW exists â that shadow was a
body `my`; the signature param should count as the same shadow.  Cheap discriminator:
`sub f ($x) { my $y = $x; $y }` (still refuses?) vs `sub f { my ($x) = @_; $x }` (same
file `my $x` after â presumably fine).  Guard row in Pl/t when fixed; full sweep is the
gate for a scoping change (CLAUDE.md WHAT-TO-RUN table).


=== s438d (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE, at the layer this task pointed to: the
signature's parameters now register with the same scope machinery a body-level
`my` uses.

TWO questions were blind to signatures, and they are the detector/rewriter pair
the project keeps ONE resolver for:
  * `_check_sub_captures` -> `_block_captures_name($child->block, â¦)` scans the
    sub's BLOCK, and a signature is a SIBLING of the block, not part of it;
  * `_ref_shadowed` (which decides whether a use is renamed along with the
    promoted file lexical) climbs to the Statement::Sub and asks
    `_stmt_declares_canon` about the preceding siblings -- the signature is one
    of them, and that predicate knew only Statement::Variable and expression-
    embedded `my`.
Both now ask `_signature_param_canons`.  Fixing only the detector would have
turned the refusal into a SILENT WRONG (the body's `$x` renamed to the file
lexical's promoted cell), which is why the pair had to move together.

PPI PRODUCES BOTH SHAPES FOR THE SAME SOURCE, and this cost the first attempt:
with `use feature "signatures"` on an EARLIER line PPI lexes `($x)` as a
PPI::Structure::Signature; on the pragma's own line it is a
PPI::Token::Prototype.  The helper accepts both (`_is_signature_node`), like
`_sub_signature_text` and `_is_pure_prototype` already do.  (The line
dependence itself is task #455.)

ONLY THE PARAMETER NAMES: a DEFAULT is an expression evaluated in the sub, so
`sub f ($x = $y)` genuinely reads the outer `$y`.  The helper splits on
TOP-LEVEL commas (a default may contain a call with its own commas) and takes
each part's LEADING symbol -- so `($x = f(1,2), @r)` declares `$x` and `@r` and
nothing else.  And the detector discounts only the canons the signature
declares: a file `my @x` with a `($x)` parameter still gates on the sub's `@x`
(guard row 7).

MEASURED: the task's four shapes (`($x)`, `($x = 1)`, `($x, @r)`, plus a nested
anon sub closing over the param) all went from "Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO:
file lexical 'x' captured by sub f" to perl's answer.  corpus-diff identical
over the 111; emission-ab over lib/**.pm + cpan-tests/** + perl's t/ = 951
files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF; **gate-SET scan over BOTH populations (638
files x2) IDENTICAL** -- the mandatory leg for a narrowed checker, since a
refusal that stops firing can turn into a silent wrong; full sweep TOTAL 18312
(+0), 0 new / 0 fixed, GATE clean (the WHAT-TO-RUN row for a scoping change);
gate 166/5767.  Guard `Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t`, 7 rows -- five both_agree
positives (including the ONE-LINE spelling, so the Token::Prototype shape is
covered), one that the file lexical declared BEFORE the sub keeps its value,
and one NEGATIVE asserting the refusal still fires for a real capture.
Inverse-guarded on a 373fd5d worktree (fails there).

RESIDUE, filed as #485 and PRE-EXISTING (identical on the worktree): a
signature DEFAULT that reads an outer lexical gets undef -- `my $y = 5; sub f
($x = $y)` gives f() where perl gives f(5).  Same root shape (the gate scans
the block, and a default is not in the block) but the opposite half, and it
needs its own decision (refuse, or promote like any other capture).
subject: REFUSAL: a signature PARAMETER `$x` plus a LATER file-level `my $x` -> "Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'x' captured by sub f" â the param is the sub's own lexical, not a capture
